He said what he said, and I don't know if somebody was telling him to say these types of things or why he would do that off the rip. Because me and him have always been very cordial and very nice to each other, and talked many times, and been respectful. So, the way he went, I was just a little surprised. "Then we had a RAF event where we were competing in the same event right after that, and I went right up to him, and I was like, 'Bro, what's your problem? Why are you talking crazy about me?' And he was like, 'You're talking about me.' And I'm like, 'I responded to you, but we're both wrestlers. We come from the same background: American wrestling. We should prop each other up. I've said nothing but kind things about you in the media, and so we should just do that.' Bo Nickal returns to face Joe Pyfer in February at UFC Cleveland. Sean Jorgensen via Getty Images "Honestly, it got kind of heated at that point, and we talked about doing a wrestling match, doing a fight, and I was like, 'Bro, what are you even talking about, man? And as heated as their altercation may have been, Nickal doesn't believe Steveson would ever fight him on the spot like the Olympian may have teased. "That sucks, and we'll see how he responds to this [loss]," Nickal said. "We'll see if he gets back on the grind, gets back to work, and the big setbacks can lead to big comebacks. So I hope that he can figure his stuff out, and I'm still, I mean, again, it's weird all the stuff between us, but I still want to root for him and want him to do well. "He's like, 'If we fought, I'd knock you out,' and I'm like, 'I'm right here, bro. I'm right here,' and he's like, ' Alright, yeah.' [He wasn't going to] do anything to me. That's the reality of it. "I never felt like we were going to fight, but it was more of an argument of what would happen if we did, and I just told him, 'You have no defense. You have no experience,' and then, obviously, that kind of was true, and we all saw what happened." Ultimately, Nickal believes people around Steveson could be the reason for the sudden jabs he's taken from Steveson. Steveson has assembled a notable crew to help him kickstart his MMA run, including all-time great former UFC champion Jon Jones. But specifically, Nickal doesn't think Jones is one at fault, as the two of them have always been cool with each other, he said. "It's just weird, because I didn't really want that beef initially," Nickal said. "I think, honestly, he's getting advice from people to go after me, because when you look at my position in the media and my position, like maybe I can be looked at as a target because a lot of casual fans think I'm privileged, 'whatever wrestler,' this, that. So maybe he's getting advice to go after me from somebody. But I don't know. It just was really out of left field to me."

item.title: Houston Rockets reshape roster with two-way contracts for Oscar Tshiebwe and Julian Phillips
item.description: Houston Rockets Julian Phillips (3) reacts to hitting a three pointer against the Oklahoma City Thunder in the second half of game action at the Toyota Center in Houston on Thursday, Oct. 15, 2026. Houston Rockets won the game 116-89. (Elizabeth Conley/Houston Chronicle) Days away from the season opener, the Houston Rockets reshaped the back end of their roster. The Rockets announced Monday that they signed center Oscar Tshiebwe and forward Julian Phillips to two-way contracts, which allow players to move between NBA teams and their G League affiliates. Each team can have up to three two-way players. Houston waived guard Sean Pedulla to make room for Tshiebwe and Phillips alongside wing Quadir Copeland. Tshiebwe, 26, is an undersized center who excels around the basket as a play finisher and offensive rebounder. In 27 NBA games with the Utah Jazz last season, he averaged 16.6 minutes, 7.8 points and 6.6 rebounds per game. In 23 G League games, he averaged 28.1 minutes, 13.6 points and 15.5 rebounds per game while shooting 58.5% from the field. Tshiebwe was the 2022 National College Player of the Year with the Kentucky Wildcats. He was also the G League's Rookie of the Year in 2024 and a two-time All-NBA G League first-team selection. Phillips, 22, is a 6-foot-7 forward from Killeen. The 35th pick in the 2023 NBA draft signed with Houston, his third NBA team, in July. He has averaged 11.4 points, 4.9 rebounds and 1.3 steals per 36 minutes in the NBA, according to the release. In 12 career G League games, Phillips has averaged 19 points, 7.4 rebounds and one steal per game while shooting 47.6% from the field and 41.4% from 3-point range. item.title: Why Ohio State’s Jeremiah Smith already ‘locked in’ as Mel Kiper Jr.’s No. 1 prospect for 2027 NFL Draft
item.description: Joseph Maiorana-Imagn Images Why Ohio State’s Jeremiah Smith already ‘locked in’ as Mel Kiper Jr.’s No. 1 prospect for 2027 NFL Draft appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Ohio State receiver Jeremiah Smith has proven to be the best player in the nation. Smith has obliterated records while at Ohio State and, now that he is eligible for the NFL Draft at the end of the season, is sure to go early. Recently, NFL Draft expert Mel Kiper Jr. named Smith the top player on his big board. Now, Kiper is reaffirming that ranking, going as far as to call it locked in, speaking with Field Yates on ESPN’s First Draft. ” I’m not trying to bait you or lead you into something, but is there any way that you can imagine Jeremiah Smith, absent an injury, not finishing as the number one player on your board?” Yates asked Kiper. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “No, it’s not going to happen. Field, I think that’s pretty much locked in. You write that in pen. He’s a great player. We’ve seen it since the freshman year where we would have probably had him in our top three to five overall big board, maybe a little higher. So we’ve been waiting for this moment this year,” Kiper said. There has long been speculation that Smith would have gone early in the 2025 NFL Draft had he not been a true freshman and not eligible to be drafted. The same likely would have happened in the 2026 NFL Draft when the Tennessee Titans took his Ohio State teammate Carnell Tate fourth overall. “When you look at Jeremiah Smith, if you say grade and he’s a 99, the next guy would probably be a 96, 97. So, nobody’s going to be touching Jeremiah Smith in terms of rating for this draft,” Kiper added “Yeah, we’ll have plenty of conversations about positional value,” Yates added. “And if the team that needs a quarterback lands the number one overall pick, would they take a quarterback or would they take Jeremiah Smith and figure out quarterback at a different time? We’re a long ways away from that.” Smith is already getting compared to Hall of Fame-level wide receivers , and the praise is fair. “I think the simplest way to put it, and somebody texted me this over the weekend, Mel, is that the comp that you often hear surrounding Jeremiah Smith is that he might be Julio Jones and even a little bit better. We’ll see,” Yates continued. “Julio Jones obviously had a Hall of Fame career in the NFL. But the fact that you can say that and the reaction from the person that hears it isn’t, ‘Stop it. That’s ridiculous. You’re crazy.”‘ The fact that the reaction is, ‘Oh, that kind of makes a little bit of sense,’ is very telling about how good of a player Jeremiah Smith is.” A wideout has not gone first overall since Keyshawn Johnson was selected first overall by the New York Jets out of USC. item.title: Wizards’ Trae Young reveals how ‘Ice Trae’ changed his taste in watches
item.description: Wizards’ Trae Young reveals how ‘Ice Trae’ changed his taste in watches appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Trae Young ’s taste in watches doesn’t always match the sparkle his nickname suggests. The Washington Wizards guard prefers understated designs, but “Ice Trae” has given him a reason to embrace diamonds. Young explained that shift while showing Robertino Altieri, CEO of WatchGuys , a watch and jewelry collection worth an estimated $2 million-plus on My Collection. “I’m more like a classy guy, more like plain Jane. But obviously, with the nickname, you kind of have to have some type of flashy thing. So I’ve gotten some things and some more iced-out watches,” Young said. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Quavo gave Young the nickname after he arrived in Atlanta. Their connection followed Young’s trips to Migos shows during his school years, adding a musical influence to a collection that also reflects his admiration for Jay-Z. The four-time All-Star credits the rapper for his interest in Hublot. His own collecting journey, though, began with a G-Shock he purchased around age 10 at an Oklahoma Best Buy. Which watches mean the most to Trae Young? Young identifies his custom blue-diamond Pristine as his favorite. WatchGuys says similar designs start around $250,000. Another Pristine in his rotation features black gems, with Altieri describing it as one of only 18 worldwide. The collection also carries meaning beyond its price tags. His wife, Shelby, celebrated two All-Star appearances with engraved Rolex watches. One includes her name alongside their children’s names, giving Young a family connection every time he wears it. Young intends to leave his collection to his children, and his son already enjoys examining the watches. He still has room for another brand. After sampling a rose-gold Patek Philippe Aquanaut, Young announced his next collecting goal: “Right now I need to add Patek to my collection.” Related: Knicks’ Jalen Brunson puts his taste to the test with new Just Salad wrap Related: Aaron Rodgers’ family finally makes it to Steelers game after reconciliation

item.title: Real Betis announce injury blow before Feyenoord clash
item.description: Real Betis announce injury blow before Feyenoord clash La Liga outfit Real Betis have early this week announced a personnel setback in the club’s attacking ranks. This comes amid confirmation that Cucho Hernández is set for an incoming spell on the sidelines. Frontman Cucho for his part featured from the off over the weekend, as Betis welcomed Barcelona to Seville for a La Liga clash. When all was said and done, Manuel Pellegrini’s troops were condemned to the wrong side of a 5-2 result. Cucho, meanwhile, was hooked from proceedings just beyond the hour mark, replaced by summer signing Troy Parrott. And as confirmed on Monday, this change came owing to an injury suffered by the Colombian earlier in the 2nd-half. As per a statement on Real Betis’ website : ‘Real Betis Balompié player Cucho Hernández suffered a muscle injury during Saturday’s match against FC Barcelona. ‘Tests he underwent this morning confirm that he has suffered damage to the left proximal soleus muscle. His reintegration into the group will depend on his progress.’ The aforementioned Troy Parrott is therefore expected to replace Cucho in the Verdiblancos’ frontline to face Feyenoord in the Champions League this week. Conor Laird – GSFN

item.title: Brandon Miller Contract Extension: Hornets Lock In $209 Million Deal
item.description: Oct 16, 2026; Memphis, Tennessee, USA; Charlotte Hornets forward Brandon Miller (24) reacts during the third quarter against the Memphis Grizzlies at FedExForum. | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Jimmy Vik The Brandon Miller contract extension is official, with the Charlotte Hornets agreeing to a five-year, $209 million rookie-scale contract extension with their forward, ESPN’s Shams Charania reported Monday, citing Miller’s representatives AJ Vaynerchuk and Joey Middleton of VaynerSports. The deal, finalized ahead of the October 19 deadline, averages roughly $41.8 million per year. At 23 and entering his fourth NBA season, Miller is now central to Charlotte’s long-term plans . Hornets Lock In Brandon Miller Contract Extension At $209 Million Oct 11, 2026; Charlotte, North Carolina, USA; Milwaukee Bucks forward Jaime Jaquez Jr. (24) guards Charlotte Hornets forward Brandon Miller (24) during the first quarter at Spectrum Center. Mandatory Credit: Scott Kinser-Imagn Images | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Jimmy Vik Oct 11, 2026; Charlotte, North Carolina, USA; Milwaukee Bucks forward Jaime Jaquez Jr. (24) guards Charlotte Hornets forward Brandon Miller (24) during the first quarter at Spectrum Center. Mandatory Credit: Scott Kinser-Imagn Images Performance That Justified the Commitment Miller posted a strong 2025–26 season, averaging 20.2 points, 4.9 rebounds, and 3.3 assists across 65 games while shooting 38.3 percent from three-point range. His improved free-throw shooting and growing playmaking responsibilities highlighted his development into a primary offensive option. He remains a valuable floor spacer with developing playmaking skills, although consistency and defensive impact remain areas for improvement. Health is another consideration. Miller underwent surgery for left shoulder instability in May 2026, making his availability and long-term durability important factors in Charlotte’s investment. The Hornets are betting that continued development, better health, and complementary pieces such as Kon Knueppel will help Miller progress toward All-Star contention. The Last Word The extension gives Charlotte a clear long-term direction, but it also raises expectations. Miller has already shown he can produce at a high level offensively. The next step is becoming more consistent, creating for others, and making a greater impact on the defensive end. Those improvements will determine whether he can make the jump from promising young scorer to genuine franchise cornerstone. At $209 million, Charlotte is betting that Miller’s best basketball is still ahead of him. If he continues to develop, the deal could give the Hornets exactly what they hoped for. If his growth stalls, the contract will become a much tougher commitment to justify. Do you think the Hornets made the right decision giving Brandon Miller a five-year, $209 million extension, or does he still have more to prove before becoming a franchise cornerstone? item.title: Aaron Boone will return as Yankees manager for 2027
item.description: PHILADELPHIA, PA - JULY 26: Aaron Boone #17 of the New York Yankees looks on from the dugout prior to the game between the New York Yankees and the Philadelphia Phillies at Citizens Bank Park on Sunday, July 26, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Rob Tringali/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images It’s official: the Yankees’ skipper will be sticking around for the 2027 season. YES Network’s Jack Curry , with credit to Bergen Record writer Pete Caldera, reported Monday that Aaron Boone will return for his 10th season as manager in the final year of his two-year, $10.5 million extension signed in 2025. Plenty of mixed opinions are already swirling in reaction to this decision, but it doesn’t come as a surprising one. Many have given their praise to Boone, including former Yankees manager Joe Girardi , for bringing the Yankees to clinch their 61st postseason berth and navigating an injury-ridden roster. During his career as manager, Boone has led the Yankees to the playoffs in eight of his nine previous seasons, albeit with just one American League pennant and a World Series appearance to show for it. They’ve fallen to the division rival Blue Jays and Rays in the ALDS during the past two seasons. The Yankees’ executives were clearly satisfied enough with Boone’s decision-making this season and chose to have him at the helm next year in hopes of bringing another championship to New York. However, with considerable levels of uncertainty at several positions this offseason, there is much to consider about how Boone will construct a winning roster. Will the Yankees give him enough ammunition to clinch a postseason spot and make it through the ALDS? More to come…

Mark Selby, Neil Robertson, Xiao Guodong, Shaun Murphy and Ali Carter fell on Sunday, with Chris Wakelin, Barry Hawkins, Trump and O'Sullivan following them out of the tournament on Monday. item.title: Braves Protect Wisely, Add Southisene To 2027 Plans
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Atlanta Braves are already building their team for 2027, according to Battery Power . They added infielder Brett Wisely to the 40-man roster on Thursday. This move protects him from being taken by other clubs. The team sent outfielder DaShawn Keirsey Jr. down to Triple-A Gwinnett. Infielder Luke Williams chose to become a free agent after being sent down. Harrison Smajovits of Atlanta Braves on SI first reported the news about Wisely. The transaction log confirms these moves happened recently. The club wants to keep their options open for next season. Wisely played 125 games for Gwinnett this year but never appeared in a big league game in 2026. He hit .281 with 11 home runs and a 127 wRC+ at the Triple-A level. Those numbers are good enough to earn a spot on the main roster now. Why the 40-Man Spot Matters Putting Wisely on the 40-man is a smart play for the organization. It stops him from using his veteran rights to leave the team for nothing. He only played four games for the big club back in 2025. That short stint did not show much, but his minor league success tells a different story. The Braves likely see him as a key part of their plans for next year. They need to protect their depth before the winter meetings start. Wisely has not been able to turn his minor league stats into big league results yet. But keeping him safe gives the team flexibility later. They could trade him or use him in a deal. The 2021 championship run taught them to value every single roster spot. Southisene Shines in Fall League While the big league roster shifts, the minor league news is also positive. Tate Southisene had a great night for the Glendale Desert Dogs in the Arizona Fall League. He reached base four times against the Surprise Saguaros. The final score was 17 to 8, a blowout win for Glendale. Southisene went 2-for-3 with a double, two walks, and a stolen base. Southisene started the game by walking and stealing second base. He scored the first run of the night on ground outs. He also hit a double that showed his power potential. The pitching in the fall league can be wild, but he waited it out. He showed the same patience that got him to Double-A early this year. He did not look rusty after the long break from play. If he keeps hitting like this, more scouts will take notice. Logan Samuels also helped the team in relief. He pitched two innings without allowing a run. He gave up two walks but struck out three batters. The pitching staff allowed 13 walks in the game, which made it sloppy. But the young hitters kept the offense moving forward. The Braves need them to step up as the big league team looks to win again.

item.description: 📋 Corinthians and Vitória line up to escape drop zone in round finale This Monday (19), Corinthians and Vitória face off at Neo Química Arena at 8 p.m. (Brasília time) in the final game of Matchday 31 of the 2026 Brasileirão. The match is a classic "six-pointer." After eight straight defeats, Timão sit just above the relegation zone in 16th place with 32 points, while Leão da Barra are 13th with 36 points. In other words, whoever wins will not only move further clear of the bottom four but also leave their opponents dangerously close to the relegation zone. Dutchman Clarence Seedorf will still be unable to take his place in the dugout to lead the São Paulo side due to paperwork issues involving his work visa and registration in the Brazilian Football Confederation's BID database. However, compared with the last match—a 4–1 defeat to Palmeiras—the 50-year-old European coach has opted to bring Angileri, Garro, Lingard and Vitinho into the Corinthians lineup in place of Matheus Bidu, Raniele, Carrilo and Depay, respectively. Jair Ventura's Vitória, coming off a 2–1 defeat to São Paulo in the previous round, are still seeking their first away win in the Brasileirão. item.title: Ashton Daniels Named ACC Quarterback of the Week
item.description: MIAMI GARDENS - OCTOBER 17: Florida State quarterback Ashton Daniels (14) passes the ball in the first quarter as the Miami Hurricanes faced the Florida State Seminoles on October 17, 2026, at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, FL. (Photo by Samuel Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images For the second time this season, fifth-year quarterback Ashton Daniels was named the the ACC Quarterback of the Week on Monday as part of the league’s weekly awards. Daniels, from Buford, Ga., accounted for five touchdowns in the Seminoles’ 43-35 double-overtime loss at No. 3 Miami on Saturday. He matched a career-high with four passing touchdowns and added a rushing touchdown, his 11th of the season to extend his FSU record for rushing touchdowns in a season by a quarterback. Daniels ranks third nationally with 23 touchdowns accounted for and is the only player with 11 passing and 11 rushing touchdowns. He has accounted for multiple touchdowns in all seven of his games as a Seminole, including a pair of five-touchdown games against Miami and Virginia, setting the FSU record with five rushing touchdowns in a game in the latter. At Miami, Daniels completed 15 passes for 298 yards and four touchdowns with 31 rushing yards and one rushing score. His final two touchdown passes went to Duce Robinson, including a 75-yard touchdown late in the fourth quarter to force overtime. Daniels, who had an 81-yard touchdown run against Virginia, is the only player in the country with a 70-yard pass and 70-yard rush this season. Entering the game, Miami ranked No. 1 nationally in scoring defense with 9.8 points allowed per game and No. 5 in total defense with 249.6 yards per game allowed. Daniels’ four passing touchdowns were more than the Hurricanes had allowed in their first five games combined (3). Daniels previously was named ACC Quarterback of the Week for his record-setting game against Virginia. The last Seminole to win ACC Quarterback of the Week multiple times in a season was Jordan Travis in 2023. After an open weekend, Florida State will be back in action on October 31 at 7:00 p.m. against Clemson in Doak Campbell Stadium.

item.title: Brighton’s latest Fabian Hurzeler stance emerges amid Man United interest
item.description: Brighton’s latest Fabian Hurzeler stance emerges amid Man United interest Brighton & Hove Albion’s position on a potential departure of their manager, Fabian Hurzeler, has come to light amidst suggestions that he is on Manchester United’s radar. Standout candidate United boss Michael Carrick is facing a fight to keep his job owing to the club’s miserable start to the 2026/27 season. Sunday’s 1-1 draw with Leeds United means that the Red Devils have now gone six games without a victory. Their last win was the 4-0 thumping of Sabah FK in the Champions League. United are currently languishing in the bottom half of the table, having gained just seven points from as many games. After the final whistle at Elland Road, Carrick acknowledged that performances and results have not been good enough but United can still enjoy a good season. It’s understood that Carrick still retains the support of the power brokers at Old Trafford. A recent report covered by The Peoples Person relayed that Carrick met with director of football Jason Wilcox, where the team’s pitiful form was addressed. Last week, Samuel Luckhurst of The Sun claimed that Hurzeler is considered the standout candidate from the Premier League to replace Carrick. Hurzeler is said to have admirers at United and his standing has only increased owing to Brighton’s sensational form this season. item.title: Davante Adams set for lengthy layoff as LA Rams rocked by injury blows
item.description: Los Angeles Rams receiver Davante Adams is expected to miss six to 10 weeks after suffering a serious hamstring injury, coach Sean McVay announced Monday. The mounting injury toll for the Rams (2-4) also includes veteran defensive tackle Poona Ford, ruled out for the year with a torn triceps, and defensive tackle Kobie Turner, headed to injured reserve with a groin problem. The preseason Super Bowl favorites have dropped three of their last four games. Adams, a six-time Pro Bowl selection who led the NFL in touchdown catches last season, sustained the injury on a noncontact play late in Sunday's 18-16 defeat to the Arizona Cardinals. On the Rams' second-to-last offensive snap, he pulled up inside the end zone before limping off the field. In his 13th NFL campaign, the 33-year-old wide receiver has recorded 30 catches for 480 yards and four touchdowns this year. Adams previously missed three late-season contests with a hamstring issue last year before coming back for postseason play. "It's significant when you don't have a player like Davante, but we have to be able to adjust," McVay said. "His contributions can't be measured. You don't replace somebody like him, and so what you've got to do is you've got to be able to figure out what's the next right thing? What does that look like in terms of our vision? We'll have to adjust and adapt." The loss of Adams leaves Los Angeles short on proven depth behind him and All-Pro wideout Puka Nacua. Konata Mumpfield currently ranks third among the team's wide receivers in production this season, tallying eight receptions for 127 yards. A reliable third receiving option was similarly lacking for Los Angeles last year, when quarterback Matthew Stafford targeted secondary wideouts less often than any rival starting signal-caller in the playoffs. Now in his second year with the Rams, nine-year NFL veteran Ford has logged just under 40% of the team's defensive snaps this term, working inside alongside Turner and Aaron Donald. While Turner plays a heavier snap load for Los Angeles, the fourth-year pro with 22 tackles this season will likewise be sidelined for "a handful of games," McVay said. McVay also confirmed that new kicker Blake Grupe is out for the season after tearing a ligament in his knee while making a tackle on kickoff coverage. Consequently, Los Angeles must recruit its third kicker of the campaign prior to visiting the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday. On a more positive note, McVay noted star cornerback Trent McDuffie is "feeling much better" following a practice injury late last week that kept him out on Sunday. A decision on McDuffie's availability against Las Vegas will be made later in the week. item.title: Rash of Rams injuries will sideline Davante Adams, Poona Ford and Kobie Turner
item.description: Rams wide receiver Davante Adams stands on the field during a game against the Buffalo Bills on Oct. 12. (Kyusung Gong / Associated Press) The Rams lost much more than a game to the Arizona Cardinals. They lost four players because of injuries. Receiver Davante Adams suffered a ruptured hamstring and will be sidelined six to 10 weeks, defensive lineman Kobie Turner suffered a groin strain and will be out several weeks and defensive lineman Poona Ford suffered a season-ending triceps injury, coach Sean McVay said Monday. Kicker Blake Grupe was placed on injured reserve after leaving Sunday’s 18-16 defeat because of a knee injury. Read more: What Super Bowl? Rams look lifeless during humbling loss to Cardinals “We’ve taken some shots this year,” McVay said during a video conference with reporters. “We’ve got to be able to get up and keep swingin’. “This is a good test.” The Rams are 2-4 heading into Sunday’s game against the Las Vegas Raiders in Las Vegas. A team that began the season as the Super Bowl favorite now must engineer turnarounds similar to those they pulled off in 2023 and 2024 to qualify for the playoffs. On Sunday, the Rams will once again be without edge rusher Myles Garrett, who has been on injured reserve because of a knee injury. McVay said the Rams would not open his 21-day window to return this week. They paid a hefty price to get him by moving Matthew Knies , and because of that, it eliminates a piece they could have used to improve their defence. Not to mention, a much larger cap hit. Auston Matthews ‘ contract is also coming to an end after the 2027-28 season, and with him being an unrestricted free agent at that time, Chayka is certainly hoping to turn the Leafs into a contender now so that their captain and the franchise’s best player doesn’t decide to leave. Mandatory Credit: Dan Hamilton-Imagn Images The issue is, most teams aren’t in the market to move a premier defenceman. And the Leafs don’t exactly have the quality pieces to acquire a top-tier defenceman either. Especially since they’ve already moved Knies and don’t want to part with Easton Cowan , so the Leafs will need to get creative. They do currently own the Colorado Avalanche’s first-round pick in the 2027 NHL Entry Draft. They also have some quality prospects like defenceman Ben Danford, goaltender Artur Akhtyamov , and forward Tinus Luc Koblar. A combination of these players and/or picks should be able to land the Leafs a solid piece. The Last Word Despite the want to add a big fish on the back end, the Maple Leafs might just not have the assets to do so. The options of players like Simon Edvinsson or Alexander Nikishin , who are currently begging to play for new teams and the Leafs have been rumoured to check in on, are more than likely a no-go based on the return Toronto would be willing to send to either Detroit or Carolina. Unless, of course, they decide they’re willing to move a player like Easton Cowan. However, that doesn’t mean they can’t improve their defence group. Names like Vince Dunn and Zach Whitecloud are two names that come to mind and are quality defencemen. They have also seen their names in the rumour mill. Dunn is currently in the last year of his contract, which carries a cap hit of $7.35 million, while Whitecloud has an extra year remaining at a much more manageable $2.75 million cap hit. Either of these players would drastically improve the Leafs’ defence group, and the Leafs most certainly could put together a package that should be able to pry them from their current teams. item.title: De Zerbi after win over Coventry: Maddison and Kulusevski have changed Spurs atmosphere
item.description: De Zerbi after win over Coventry: Maddison and Kulusevski have changed Spurs atmosphere Roberto De Zerbi hailed the impact of James Maddison and Dejan Kulusevski after Tottenham beat Coventry City 3-1, insisting their presence has changed the atmosphere around the squad. Maddison, who opened the scoring, started his first game in more than 500 days for Tottenham, while Kulusevski returned to action off the bench after around a year-and-a-half out. “Very happy for the result, very happy for Maddison, and very happy for Kulusevski,” De Zerbi said. “I think we played much better in other games, Old Trafford or against Aston Villa especially in the first half, Everton especially in the first half, Liverpool in the Carabao Cup, but credit to Coventry. “They are different players, different talent, different experience, different personality. “With them in the dressing room there is another atmosphere.” De Zerbi believes the victory was important not only for the three points, but also for the belief it can give his side. “The result is important but I think the most important thing can be two things,” he said. “The first one, we understood we are able to win a game like other teams in the Premier League, and the second one if we put something more than ourselves, like we have done in the last two weeks.” The Spurs boss also revealed he held a significant meeting with his players before the recent draw with Manchester United. “The day before Old Trafford, we had a big meeting and spoke about the situation, that we can’t accept or move on if we don’t take more responsibility,” De Zerbi said. “This week was important because we stayed together, spent time together, and they worked to build not a family but like a family. “During the game, if you have a problem and there is a tough situation, you have to play for your team-mate, your friend, your brother, not like robots.” De Zerbi also explained that Kulusevski’s late introduction was partly for the supporters, who had waited a long time to see the Swede back on the pitch. “I called for Kulusevski just for the fans,” he said. “They waited for him to come on the pitch and in the last five or ten minutes and extra time, we needed that support from the fans. “They were fantastic with Kulusevski, with us. “They suffered too much in the last two, three, four seasons, I don’t know, but they deserve to celebrate.”

item.title: Annika Sorenstam, husband played match against their kids ahead of LPGA event
item.description: Annika Sorenstam got an early look at Pelican Golf Club ahead of her namesake LPGA event next month. And for a course that has seen its share of showdowns – including Capital One's The Match – this contest was particularly close to the heart. Sorenstam and husband Mike McGee took on a couple of high school golfers – their two kids, Ava and Will – for a friendly match-up last Saturday. View this post on Instagram Ava, a senior at Lake Highland Prep, who joined the golf team this fall , shot 85 from the forward tees while Will, playing from the tips, posted 75. Mom and dad shot even par and 81 respectively, from combo tees at about 6,500 yards. Will, who has big goals in the game and plays with mom annually at the PNC Championship, is a left-handed player while Ava, a softball player, plays golf right-handed. “She has quite a lot of clubhead speed,” said Sorenstam earlier this year at the U.S. Senior Women's Open. “You know, she’s working around the green. She can hit par 4s in one and then walk away with six.” Mom also reports that Ava has put in the work, high praise coming from an athlete known for her meticulous work ethic. At last year's PNC, 15-year-old Will was slightly shorter than his mom and now has almost caught up to dad. He recently finished eighth in the 13-15 flight of the FJT Tour Championship with a closing 69. Sorenstam, a 72-time winner on the LPGA, will once again host the current best in the world for the penultimate event of the season. The Annika driven by Gainbridge at Pelican will be played Nov. 12-15 in Belleair, Florida, and will be headlined No. 1 Nelly Korda, who will be vying for her fourth title at the event. "The course looks incredible and the energy is already building up," Sorenstam wrote in an Instagram post. After the match, 56-year-old Sorenstam took in her first Tampa Bay Buccaneers game against the Pittsburgh Steelers. The family chatted with good friend Aaron Rodgers on the sideline ahead of Pittsburgh's overtime win. Tournament sponsor EMaxx hosted Sorenstam and her family in its Raymond James Stadium suite, and she was announced to the crowd on the Jumbotron. Beth Ann Nichols is a Golfweek senior writer covering the LPGA and women's golf. item.title: Liam Lawson eyes joining Vettel and Bottas at major motorsport event in 2027
item.description: Liam Lawson has revealed that he would welcome the chance to compete in the 2027 Race of Champions, which will take place in his native New Zealand for the first time. The Racing Bulls driver could potentially join several established Formula 1 names at the event in Wellington. The competition is scheduled for 9-10 January at Hnry Stadium, with Sebastian Vettel and Valtteri Bottas already confirmed among the participants. Lawson has not yet been announced as part of the line-up, but his plans for the winter could allow him to attend. Speaking to GPblog and other media, the New Zealander acknowledged that he was interested in taking part, although his participation remains uncertain: "I'm not actually sure yet, but it looks like something that'll be really, really cool. I should be there over at that time as well, so it'd be something I'd love to do." Lawson could face familiar F1 names in New Zealand Should Lawson secure a place on the entry list, he could find himself competing against four-time world champion Vettel, who has previously enjoyed considerable success at the Race of Champions. Bottas will also participate, while Supercars champion Chaz Mostert and New Zealand rally driver Hayden Paddon are among the other confirmed names. Photo: Red Bull Content Pool Photo: Red Bull Content Pool The event will feature competitors from several major racing championships, including Formula 1, the World Rally Championship, IndyCar and NASCAR. Rather than competing in their usual machinery, drivers will race identical cars on a specially constructed circuit inside the stadium. Two separate competitions will be held across the weekend: the individual Race of Champions, which determines the Champion of Champions, and the Nations Cup, in which drivers compete for their respective countries. The event has previously welcomed numerous Formula 1 stars, including Michael Schumacher, Fernando Alonso and Lando Norris. For Lawson, taking part would mean racing in front of his home crowd, something he has never had the opportunity to experience in Formula 1, as New Zealand does not feature on the calendar. The 24-year-old has previously competed in several championships around the world, but an appearance at the Race of Champions would offer a different experience, particularly with the event taking place in his home country. Despite expressing his interest, Lawson has not yet confirmed whether he will participate. With the event scheduled for January, during Formula 1's winter break, there would be no direct clash with a Grand Prix weekend.

item.title: CBS’ Leger Douzable ponders message Eagles are sending with handling of Jalen Hurts
item.description: Credit: CBS Sports News broke Monday morning that Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts would miss the rest of the season after further testing revealed several blood clots in his lungs. The story took another turn when Tom Pelissero of The Ringer and Netflix, who initially broke the news, followed up with a report that Hurts played against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London last week after having already been diagnosed. “How committed is Jalen Hurts to football? After initially being diagnosed with a superficial blood clot in London, doctors told him not to sleep as a precaution, so he had been awake for roughly 36 hours when he started against the Jaguars, throwing for 220 yards and a TD,” the insider wrote on X. Pelissero’s reporting raised obvious questions across sports media about why Hurts was allowed to take the field against Jacksonville after 36 hours without sleeping, and also why the quarterback was allowed to fly home with active blood clots, which can be incredibly dangerous. Pelissero later clarified that he spoke with Hurts’ agent, Nicole Lynn, who confirmed Hurts was allowed to sleep after rejoining the team and that the stadium set aside a room for him to rest. Even so, the decision to let him take the field warrants scrutiny. CBS NFL analyst Leger Douzable went so far as to call the Eagles’ handling of the situation “disturbing” and questioned what message it sends to other players in the league about how the organization operates. “This is why this is so disturbing, because this is a guy that has been to two Super Bowls for your organization, won one, and in both of those games he was the best player on the field. If you’re treating this guy like this, what does that message send to the rest of the players in that locker room?” Douzable asked. “If you’re treating [Jalen Hurts] like this, what does that message send to other players in that locker room? This is the face of our franchise, and you have to protect the warrior, the competitor, against themselves sometimes.” The former NFL defensive end went on to hold the Eagles to account not only because of the dangers of playing with active blood clots and without having slept for 36 hours, but also for reportedly allowing him to play despite having found out the blood clots spread from his calf to his lungs. “And then, from what I’ve been reading, they found out that it did spread up to his lungs, and he still played in that game,” he said. “So this is 100% on the Philadelphia Eagles, and it’s disturbing that they allowed the face of the franchise, or any player, right?” Douzable wrapped up the segment by saying the Eagles should’ve responded differently after Hurts’ diagnosis.

item.description: European governing body gives two-week deadline Letter addresses other issues including Balogun affair Uefa has given Fifa a two-week deadline to release key documents relating to Gianni Infantino’s World Cup sell-off plan and other governance issues in its latest critique of football’s world governing body . A letter sent to Fifa’s general secretary, Mattias Grafström, by his counterpart at Uefa, Theodore Theodoridis, is accompanied by an eight-page document that has more than 50 questions about Fifa’s handling of dozens of issues over the past 12 months. These include the proposed sale of 20% of its commercial rights, the Folarin Balogun affair , the peace prize and relations with Donald Trump and the arrangements for next year’s Fifa presidential election. Uefa’s document also makes a number of allegations about potential conflicts of interests at Fifa, as well as repeating calls for a “genuinely independent” governance review. Continue reading...

Vincent Kompany’s low profile on the Allianz Arena touchline, almost motionless in his seat as his team rattled a flurry of goals past poor RB Leipzig, had nothing to do with any lingering chagrin connected to those slow starts from his team. item.title: Houthi conflict casts shadow as Saudi Arabia scales back sporting pipe dreams
item.description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling Cristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Guardiola returns to Manchester as City spin into dizzy mess against PSG
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! It is quite funny that PSG felt like the good guys at the Etihad Stadium but if we briefly detach ourselves from the notion that the European champions’ own sportswashing and cashsplashing has also done immeasurable damage to the beautiful game, then their 4-2 Bigger Cup shellacking of Manchester City was pure cinema, baby! I was stunned at reading the comments in support of Manchester City keeping their trophies, coming out of the mouth of their Bigger Cup rivals at PSG (yesterday’s Quote of the Day). Given the example of the organisers of the Tour de Lance … sorry, the Tour de France, this kind of ‘keep the awards you won’ stuff might get him sent to the Bastille. Or consider Formula One. They’ve got all kinds of rules about driver behaviour on the racetrack, and additional rules about what the crew can and cannot do to your car. Cars get inspected before each race, and there are also mandatory post-race inspections for every car. You might drive your car first across the line to the cheers of the crowd, but if the post-race inspection discovered that you cheated in how your team designed your vehicle, your memory of crossing the line is all you get to keep. Think about that for a minute. If the Premier League and Fifa cannot clear the bar for morals in sport set by the UCI and FIA, that says a lot. And none of it good” – Peter Rehwaldt. My friend Bernard grew up in Coventry. And as a boy he thought the team was called ‘Coventry City Nil’. I would get out more, but I’m a Manchester United fan” – Brendan Hughes. item.description: Former Manchester City player is coming out of retirement at 40 to play one match for ambitious Supreme Sha Tin Hong Kong, China (as is the official football name), has long tried to follow the advice of Han Solo in Return of the Jedi: keeping their distance from China while trying not to look like they are keeping their distance. It is all about maintaining an independent football association and the trappings and privilege that come with it. There was some talk a few years ago about getting a Hong Kong team in the Chinese Super League, when the spending was in full flow, and although that did not happen the local Premier League has belatedly got in on the act – kind of. This glittering city is not known as a football hotbed but has a long history in the sport that started when it was a British colony and has continued since it became a special administrative region of China in 1997. George Best, Peter Shilton, Arie Haan, Bobby Moore, Diego Forlán, Nicky Butt, René van de Kerkhof, Tony Morley, Gordon McQueen and Craig Foster have played in the territory and soon David Silva will too. item.description: The winger is 28, and younger teammates are rising into the high-pressure spots he has usually occupied Usually, the second weekend of October sees Christian Pulisic flanked by compatriots as the Star-Spangled Banner plays. item.description: It’s not just that the club’s recent charges themselves are unprecedented – it’s the language used to describe them too Sign up for our free newsletter here The language of football is a fine and highly nuanced dialect. The majority of people involved in the game speak it with a high degree of sophistication. Minor deviations from the familiar, almost imperceptible to outsiders, can set off alarm bells: what’s really going on there? Why isn’t he happy? What’s she hinting at? But it’s an argot developed to talk about football, and when applied to other subjects, it can sound extremely jarring. Erling Haaland is one of the brighter, more engaging players. There’s an appealing quirkiness to him that suggests he has a higher-than-usual level of self-awareness. He doesn’t mind stepping outside the norms, being a bit different. item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.description: Manchester City unrepentant in victory, Spurs make progress of a sort and Noni Madueke meets the moment The manner of Manchester City’s victory at Liverpool was an article of both vindication and vilification. The same went for City players, asked to perform under the darkest of clouds, able to focus, at last, on football, rather than legal argument and uncertain futures. Beyond City, the sight of a club found guilty of 100-plus charges laying waste to such rivals as Liverpool was deeply uncomfortable . The Premier League season and product are badly damaged until the matter is somehow resolved. What happened at Anfield should double the haste for a resolution. item.title: Why we’re stuck with a Premier League in the clutches of the global mega-rich | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s little prospect of the model changing in a country that welcomes wealthy international owners with open arms Football, the world’s most popular sport, played by laws drawn up in London in 1863. The Premier League is the UK’s greatest soft power export. Premier League clubs are owned by a deputy prime minister of Abu Dhabi, the public investment fund of Saudi Arabia, a billionaire based in Monaco for tax reasons and a disappointing assortment of investors and private equity funds. And what, really, could be more British than that? Football truly is the national game. What the Manchester City case has exposed is just how difficult it is to regulate some of the richest and most powerful bodies in the world. While the wait for the verdict was frustrating, it was perhaps unavoidable given the possibility of legal objection at every turn when a leaked email from City’s in-house lawyer during Uefa’s action against the club had threatened to “ spend 30 million on the 50 best lawyers in the world to sue them for the next 10 years”. You didn’t get that with Albert Alexander Sr or Peter Swales. Continue reading...

item.title: Lionel Messi’s Argentina career turned football into a sacred mystery
item.description: Jorge Messi wanted his country to fall in love with his son. That ambition was fulfilled during a brilliant international career that ended this week “What Argentina is doing in this World Cup is of a sacred order,” Brazilian writer Milly Lacombe posted at the height of the tide of anti-Argentinian sentiment during this year’s tournament. She was exploring the contradiction she felt around her support of Lionel Messi: “a player who is a God and a man who shakes Trump’s hand”. Lacombe highlighted the importance of acknowledging the complexities around Messi and the Argentinian team. How is it possible that Messi was not speaking out against the racist incidents we all saw around the Argentina team , she asked. “That’s why it hurts so much to see someone with Messi’s power choosing to make himself small,” she wrote. item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
